title: Conditional Irrationality of All Projective Stabilizations of Cubic Threefolds: Point-Class Rank under Quantum Wall Crossing
description: Assuming a gauged-admissible marked Wlodarczyk completion and the inverse-system family of one-object marked threshold comparisons stated in this paper, X × P^m is irrational for every smooth complex cubic threefold X and every m ≥ 0. The endpoint contrast is unconditional: the paper reconstructs the primitive-sixth block from Cai's matrices, proves Gamma point-row nonvanishing by a Barnes calculation, and shows that multiplication by P^m produces m + 1 copies and preserves detection of the resulting packet while projective space has no primitive-sixth packet. It also proves an exact ambient point-column identity for a simple VGIT wall, exact Gamma point-row transport across an ordinary flop, global support collapse under the gauged-admissibility assumptions, and a coefficientwise balanced Gamma-ratio reduction. A rank-one derived-intersection theorem identifies the fixed clutching stacks and their perfect obstruction theories along every affine tail between thresholds, making complete neutral tails holonomic with tempered growth. Beyond gauged-admissibility, the remaining unproved input is a family over all finite Artin levels, ordinary degrees, neutral directions, and thresholds. At each threshold one marked local Fourier object must induce the comparison of finite cyclic Rees z-differential modules; zero-mode thresholds use row-generated reduced nearby cycles. The comparisons must intertwine formal monodromy, carry the marked point row, preserve the stated Stokes, deck, Artin, and Rees data, and identify the entire adjacent row-generated cyclic module with its reduced nearby-cycle realization. Preservation of primary support then follows by polynomial functional calculus. A rational two-tail counterexample and the other countermodels explain why tailwise holonomicity, formal monodromy, pairing, integrality, and localized Fourier support do not replace that marked compatibility.
